Australian Big Four Banks Hold Billions in Zero-Interest Accounts As Savings Conditions Draw Scrutiny

01 Nov 2026, 02:58 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.abc.net.au

2 min read

Key takeawaysRecent annual reports from Australia’s major financial institutions indicate that billions of dollars from customers remain parked in transaction and savings accounts yielding little to no interest. According to the published reports:

Overview of Bank Deposits

Recent annual reports from Australia’s major financial institutions indicate that billions of dollars from customers remain parked in transaction and savings accounts yielding little to no interest. According to the published reports:

  • Commonwealth Bank: Held approximately $122 billion as of June in accounts yielding no interest.
  • Westpac: Held approximately $82 billion as of March.
  • National Australia Bank (NAB): Held approximately $67 billion.
  • ANZ: Held approximately $61 billion.

Data compiled by financial comparison site Canstar indicates that following previous rate adjustments by the Reserve Bank of Australia, the major banks adjusted their maximum savings rates by 0.20 or 0.25 percentage points.

Reported Consumer Concerns

Consumer advocacy groups have raised concerns regarding the conditions attached to high-interest savings products. Reports highlight that accounts offering higher returns frequently require regular deposits and minimum monthly balances. Failure to meet these criteria often results in accounts reverting to a baseline rate of 0.10 percent, which yields near-zero returns.

Findings from a 2023 retail deposit inquiry by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) suggested that a significant majority of customers—specifically over 70 percent—frequently miss monthly conditions. Furthermore, Canstar data indicates low consumer migration between institutions, with only 16 percent of consumers switching savings accounts and 11 percent changing transaction accounts over a three-year period.

Perspectives from Experts and Industry Bodies

Canstar spokesperson Sally Tindall stated that the mechanics of how banks pass on rate increases can lack transparency, leaving many customers vulnerable to missed criteria.

Western Sydney University Associate Professor Michelle Cull advised consumers to regularly review their banking arrangements and carefully examine terms and conditions.

Conversely, Australian Banking Association Chief Executive Simon Birmingham stated that banks assist customers in maximizing their savings returns, noting that institutions paid out more than $120 billion in interest to depositors over the previous financial year.

Practical Implications and Verification

Consumers assessing their financial products may consider the following steps:

  • Review existing account terms and conditions, particularly monthly deposit requirements and withdrawal restrictions.
  • Compare current savings rates and term deposit options across multiple financial institutions.
  • Monitor alerts and communications issued by banking providers.
  • Verify original announcements by consulting official bank annual reports, independent comparison data from Canstar, and original reporting from ABC News.
